Everything on the shelves

24 titles and 43 lives. Every figure carries its source.

The Press · ideas

  • Compounding MachinesA few research organisations produced the century. The structure was the invention.
  • The Scaling CurveCapability became forecastable from spend. That turned research into capital allocation.
  • Silicon & LightMoore's Law was never a law. It was a schedule everyone agreed to believe.
  • The Unix BargainComposability bought with discoverability. Fifty years on, still the best trade in software.
  • The BoxThe container was not a technology problem. It was a standards and labour problem.
  • The Great DivergenceThe best unsettled argument in economics, and every industrial policy implicitly picks a side.
  • Finding LongitudeA prize specified an outcome, not a method. It took sixty years and nobody won it.
  • The Republic of LettersPeer review was invented as an administrative convenience by an overworked secretary.
  • Movable TypeCities that got a press grew faster. Everything about why is still argued.
  • Being Wrong ProductivelyState in advance what would change your mind. Everything else is decoration.
  • In Defense of BubblesSome infrastructure only gets built by people who are collectively, temporarily wrong.
  • Money Is a LedgerThe interesting question is never 'is it money'. It's whose ledger, and who can reverse an entry.
  • The Cost DiseaseHalf of it is a feature of growth. Half of it is a choice. The mix is the argument.
  • Comparative AdvantageTrue, non-trivial, two centuries old, and still argued against by people who understand it.
  • Why Firms ExistIf markets allocate so well, why is your company not a market? Coase asked at 21.
  • The Concept of LawA legal system is a union of primary and secondary rules — and the master rule is a social fact.
  • The Heated DiskGeometry is not true or false. It is convenient — and Poincaré built a toy world to prove it.
  • The Banking ModelEducation is never neutral: it either domesticates or liberates. Freire's claim, and the fight it started.
  • The Plastic TideWe measured the tide before we understood the water. What microplastics do to us is genuinely unknown — which is not the same as safe.
  • Water in the WestThe American West is not arid land with some cities on it. It is a plumbing project with a civilisation attached.
  • The Baptism and the ChainReference is inherited, not earned. If that is true for us, it may be true for the machines trained on what we wrote.
  • Forty-TwoThe joke is not that the answer is meaningless. It is that nobody wrote down the question.
  • The Listening ListSeven free pieces, about four hours total, disproportionately load-bearing.
  • Open QuestionsFive places where my own sources contradict each other, kept visible on purpose.
